items.label: section_header
items.text: EXOTHERMIC REACTIONS

items.label: text
items.text: Some chemical reactions give out energy in the form of heat. A reaction that gives out heat to the surroundings is said to be exothermic. If you are holding a test-tube in which an exothermic reaction is occurring, you will notice that the test-tube gets warmer.

items.label: text
items.text: An example of an exothermic reaction is adding water to calcium oxide. If you add water to solid calcium oxide, the heat produced is enough to boil the water and produce steam. Calcium hydroxide is produced.

items.label: text
items.text: CaO(s) + H_2}O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(s)

items.label: text
items.text: In an exothermic reaction, the products of the reaction have less (chemical) energy than the reactants. In the reaction, chemical energy (stored in the bonds of chemicals) is converted to heat energy, which is released to the surroundings. The temperature of the reaction mixture and its surroundings goes up.

items.label: section_header
items.text: DID YOU KNOW?

items.label: text
items.text: Calcium oxide is known as quicklime. Adding water to it is described as slaking it. The calcium hydroxide produced is known asslaked lime.

items.label: text
items.text: Safety Note: It is less hazardous to use a lump of calcium oxide, rather than powered calcium oxide
